title: FedPEFT-IMU — Experimental Results

encoders.name: limu_bert
encoders.pretrained_source: Official LIMU-BERT weights pretrained on HHAR (phones + smartwatches)

encoders.name: ssl_wearables
encoders.pretrained_source: Official Oxford harnet10 weights, self-supervised on UK-Biobank wrist data

encoders.name: unimts
encoders.architecture: ST-GCN, 10 graph blocks over a 22-joint skeleton, 64-512 channels
encoders.pretrained_source: Official UniMTS weights (motion-capture-synthesised IMU aligned with text)

encoders.name: halo
encoders.architecture: Patch-channel Transformer, 8 alternating temporal/channel layers, d=192
encoders.pretrained_source: Our re-implementation, self-supervised (MAE + patch contrastive) on the Capture-24 pool users

methods.name: fedavg_scratch
methods.label: FedAvg from scratch
methods.description: Random initialisation; the whole model is trained and uploaded every round.

methods.name: v0_full_ft
methods.label: V0 · Full fine-tuning
methods.description: Pretrained encoder; the whole model is fine-tuned and uploaded (upper-cost baseline).

methods.name: v1_head_only
methods.label: V1 · Head only
methods.description: Frozen pretrained encoder; only the heads g and h are trained and uploaded (lower-cost baseline).

methods.name: v2_lora_naive
methods.label: V2 · LoRA, naive avg
methods.description: LoRA (r=8) + heads; the server averages A and B separately: avg(B)·avg(A).

methods.name: v3_lora_exact
methods.label: V3 · LoRA, exact avg
methods.description: LoRA (r=8) + heads; exact FedEx-LoRA aggregation avg(B·A), residual folded into W0.

methods.name: v4_hetero_rank
methods.label: V4 · Heterogeneous ranks
methods.description: Device tiers train LoRA ranks 2/4/8; zero-pad, exact aggregation, SVD re-factorisation.

methods.name: v5_proposed
methods.label: V5 · FedPEFT-IMU (proposed)
methods.description: V4 + local norm + local input adapter + personal head + class-prototype alignment.

findings: Centralized from scratch, HALO is the strongest architecture (macro-F1 0.623). Starting from the pretrained weights improves every encoder: LIMU-BERT +0.090, ssl-wearables +0.135, UniMTS +0.091, HALO +0.048 macro-F1.

Training from scratch in the federation (non-IID users, 20 % participation) loses LIMU-BERT 0.183, ssl-wearables 0.291, UniMTS 0.334, HALO 0.273 macro-F1 against centralized training from scratch. This is the gap the pretrained encoders are meant to close.

FedPEFT-IMU (V5) against full fine-tuning (V0), macro-F1: LIMU-BERT 0.426 vs 0.271 with 9x less uplink; ssl-wearables 0.706 vs 0.613 with 50x less uplink; UniMTS 0.549 vs 0.537 with 36x less uplink; HALO 0.600 vs 0.510 with 92x less uplink.

Federated LoRA without personalisation (best of V2/V3) against V0: LIMU-BERT V2 0.265 vs V0 0.271; ssl-wearables V2 0.695 vs V0 0.613; UniMTS V2 0.458 vs V0 0.537; HALO V3 0.379 vs V0 0.510. LoRA matches or beats full fine-tuning for LIMU-BERT, ssl-wearables; for UniMTS, HALO the frozen features need more than a low-rank update in this round budget.

Exact LoRA aggregation (V3) versus naive averaging (V2), macro-F1 difference: LIMU-BERT -0.001, ssl-wearables -0.015, UniMTS -0.007, HALO +0.007. In this setting the naive error is small (see the aggregation-error chart) and does not cost accuracy. Exact aggregation must ship the dense residual to every client: downlink per round is LIMU-BERT 2x, ssl-wearables 34x, UniMTS 23x, HALO 10x that of V2.
LoRA rank (ssl-wearables, V3): r=2 0.702, r=4 0.695, r=8 0.680, r=16 0.673. The best rank is r=2 at 0.51 MB per client-round; a larger rank does not buy accuracy here.
Highest worst-10 % client F1 per encoder: LIMU-BERT V5 0.209; ssl-wearables V2 0.435 (V5 0.356); UniMTS V0 0.394 (V5 0.243); HALO V0 0.352 (V5 0.317).

New users, zero-shot (V5 = nearest global prototype with the default normalisation, as in the plan): LIMU-BERT V5 0.294 vs V3 0.311; ssl-wearables V5 0.369 vs V3 0.602; UniMTS V5 0.284 vs V3 0.518; HALO V5 0.497 vs V3 0.475. Where V5 falls behind, the personal normalisation it trained with is missing for a new user; 1-5 minutes of labels let V5 adapt its norm and head (see section 5).

For 9 of 28 federated models, 5 minutes of labels score below zero-shot. The models with the weaker half of zero-shot scores gain +0.093 on average from 5 minutes of labels, the stronger half changes by -0.007. This is consistent with a class-prior shift: the few-shot sample is roughly class-balanced while real days are dominated by sleep and sitting. A prior correction or regularised fine-tuning is the obvious next step.
Budget note: UniMTS ran with a reduced compute budget (see the callouts), so compare its methods with each other.
All numbers come from one user split (seed 0). Differences of a few F1 points should be confirmed with the 'full' profile (3 held-out lists) before they are claimed.
